question: In relation to cartilage:

options.opa: Type I collagen predominates in hyaline.
options.opb: Chondrocytes form small groups called aggrecans.
options.opc: The epiphyseal disc is fibrous cartilage.
options.opd: The cartilage has two types of growth: apposition and interstitial.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hyaline cartilage is primarily composed of collagen" -> "Type II collagen predominates in hyaline cartilage" -> "Type I collagen is not predominant in hyaline" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Chondrocytes are the cells found in cartilage" -> "Chondrocytes do not form groups called aggrecans" -> "Aggrecans are large proteoglycans, not groups of chondrocytes" -> 80%
CHAIN: "The epiphyseal disc is a growth plate" -> "The epiphyseal disc is made of hyaline cartilage" -> "Hyaline cartilage is not fibrous cartilage" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Cartilage can grow in two ways" -> "Appositional growth adds new layers to the surface" -> "Interstitial growth increases the size from within" -> 95%
analysis: Hyaline cartilage primarily contains Type II collagen, not Type I. Chondrocytes do not form groups called aggrecans; aggrecans are large proteoglycans found in cartilage. The epiphyseal disc, or growth plate, is made of hyaline cartilage, not fibrous cartilage. Cartilage does indeed grow by apposition (growth from the outside) and interstitial (growth from within) methods.
